title: Strategy's bitcoin buying hinges on one number: STRC at $100
body: What is happening Strategy, the largest corporate holder of bitcoin, bought no bitcoin in the week of October 19 to 25. Instead it spent $204.9 million buying back its own STRC preferred shares, according to its October 26 filing with the SEC. Those buybacks have helped lift STRC to about $99.36, its highest level in roughly five months and just shy of its $100 par value. Social media accounts have run with the next step: Michael Saylor is "set to resume heavy Bitcoin buying" once STRC gets back to $100. That claim rests on a real, stated plan. Whether it plays out as "heavy" is a different question, and readers may get some answers soon. Strategy reports third-quarter results after the US close on Thursday, October 29, with a webinar at 5:00 p.m. Eastern Time. What STRC is and why $100 matters STRC, nicknamed Stretch, is a perpetual preferred share with a variable dividend that Strategy pays monthly. The dividend is adjusted to keep the price anchored near its $100 par value, and Strategy raised the rate to 12% during the summer slump. The $100 level matters because Strategy has said it will not sell new STRC below par. Above it, STRC becomes a fundraising tool again: Strategy can sell shares into the market and use the cash to buy bitcoin. It still has about $17.5 billion of STRC available to sell under its at-the-market (ATM) programme, and that figure has not moved in its weekly filings since at least June. Management has been explicit about the link.

title: PBOC is expected to set the USD/CNY reference rate at 6.6596 – Reuters estimate
body: The People's Bank of China is due to set the daily USD/CNY reference rate at around 0115 GMT (2115 US Eastern time), a fixing that remains one of the most closely watched signals in Asian foreign exchange markets. China operates a managed floating exchange rate system, under which the renminbi (yuan) is allowed to trade within a prescribed band around a central reference rate, or midpoint, set each trading day by the PBOC. The current trading band permits the currency to move plus or minus 2% from the official midpoint during onshore trading hours. Each morning, the PBOC determines the midpoint based on a range of inputs. These include the previous day's closing price, movements in major currencies, particularly the US dollar, broader international FX conditions, and domestic economic considerations such as capital flows, growth momentum and financial stability objectives. The midpoint is not a purely mechanical calculation, allowing policymakers discretion to guide market expectations. Once the midpoint is announced, onshore USD/CNY is free to trade within the allowable band. If market pressures push the yuan toward either edge of that range, the central bank may step in to smooth volatility. Intervention can take the form of direct buying or selling of yuan, adjustments to liquidity conditions, or guidance through state-owned banks. As a result, the daily fixing is often interpreted as a policy signal rather than just a technical reference point.

title: Much ado about nothing? Fed chair Warsh talks up a storm but December rate hike bets barely budge
body: After all that waiting and wondering, what exactly did we learn from the Fed yesterday? Judging by the market reaction and pricing, I would say not a whole lot. Fed chair Warsh spent a good chunk of time talking, even though it was a shortened press conference, yet December rate hike expectations did not materially change by much. All in all, quite the productive afternoon for the central bank, eh? If I had to pack all of it in a sentence, I'd call it a whole lot of nothing for December market pricing but not necessarily a meaningless Fed meeting. Prior to the decision, traders had priced in roughly 88% odds of a 25 bps rate hike for December. And now after Warsh's press conference? That sits roughly around 82% odds. If terms of basis points, that's just a shift from roughly 22 bps to approximately 20 bps now. So, that's not really saying much. The Fed did upgrade its assessment of economic growth from "solid" to "strong", while two policymakers dissented in favour of an immediate rate hike. Hammack was perhaps expected but Cook was a bit of a surprise, though it wasn't anything major come what may. In any case, those can be interpreted as hawkish signals but Warsh wasn't exactly quick to embrace them. Instead, he chose to argue that stronger productivity could help explain why resilient economic growth doesn't necessarily translate into more inflation. Adding that with previous tightening already starting to bite, there's good reason not to rush another move for now.

The earnings did at least signal that growth is there, but just how much is it really going to cost to keep that growth going? That is the question. title: ES - 2026-10-29 - Damien Klossner, Igor Mlikota and Sabrina Stadelmann: What collateral is used in the Swiss interbank repo market?
body: Collateral is a key component of repurchase agreement transactions. We document collateral usage in the Swiss interbank repo market using an extensive transaction-level dataset. We find that a substantial share of securities eligible for the SNB General Collateral Basket is actively used, particularly securities denominated in Swiss francs. Collateral usage is concentrated in a small number of issuers and highly rated securities denominated in Swiss francs. At the same time, it displays a broad and balanced maturity profile, and cross-currency repos account for a meaningful share of trading volume.

title: US GDP Advance for the 3rd quarter 3.4% vs 3.2% estimate
body: Prior quarter 2,2% The details GDP: 3.4% vs 3.2% expected. Prior revised to 2.2% from 1.5%. Real final sales: 1.7% vs 2.0% expected. Prior 2.8% Consumer spending: 3.8%. Prior 3.8%. GDP deflator: 2.2% vs 3.5% expected. Prior 6.1% Core PCE prices: 2.5% vs 2.4% expected. Prior 3.3% PCE prices: 2.1% vs 2.6% expected. Prior 5.0% What drove the GDP increase? The 3.4% increase in Q3 GDP was supported by investment, consumer spending and government spending. Trade was the main drag, with exports falling and imports rising. Investment was the largest positive contributor, adding 3.27% to growth. That category includes business investment, housing and changes in inventories. Consumer spending added roughly 2.52%, reinforcing the importance of household demand to the expansion. Government spending added 0.90%, providing another source of support. Lower exports subtracted 0.68%, reflecting a decline in sales of US-produced goods and services abroad. Higher imports subtracted 2.64%. Imports are deducted because GDP measures domestic production, while spending on imported products is included elsewhere in the accounts. The takeaway is that domestic spending carried the economy while trade weighed heavily on growth. Investment was a major support, but the distinction between productive investment and inventory accumulation matters. With final sales growing more slowly than headline GDP, the sustainability of the inventory contribution will be something to watch.

US Jobless Claims measure the number of people filing for unemployment benefits and provide a timely indicator of labour market conditions. Initial claims track new applications and offer insight into layoffs, while continuing claims measure the number of people still receiving benefits, providing clues about how easily unemployed workers find new jobs. title: Why markets often move in the opposite direction to the news?
body: One of the most confusing aspects of financial markets for new traders is that prices often move in the opposite direction to what the news suggest. Stocks can fall after strong economic data, gold can fall despite geopolitical tensions, and bonds can rise following an inflation surprise. The most important thing to know is that markets react to how new information changes expectations, not whether the news is good or bad. Financial markets are forward-looking. Prices reflect what traders collectively expect to happen over the coming months, meaning much of the anticipated impact of an economic release or policy decision may be already priced in. What matters the most is how the actual outcome compares to what the market expected. For example, if markets expect the Federal Reserve to signal two more rate hikes, the US dollar could still fall if the central bank delivers on expectations, simply because the outcome was already expected. If the Fed, on the other hand, signals more rate hikes than expected, the greenback can rally hard as markets reprice expectations. Ever heard the term "good news is bad news"? Well, economic data can affect multiple variables simultaneously. Stronger growth, for instance, can support corporate earnings while increasing inflationary pressures and reducing the likelihood of monetary easing. Suppose US economic activity accelerates unexpectedly.

title: Google stock analysis after earnings: Is AI eating into search profits?
body: Google's AI may be cannibalizing search. Can Gemini pay the bill? More AI usage does not guarantee more profit. Alphabet's latest results sharpen a question for investors: can advertising and subscriptions replace the value of the searches AI absorbs? Analysis | October 29, 2026 | Alphabet: GOOGL and GOOG Google stock is getting hammered almost 11% in pre-market. For today, I'm watching $280-$284 for a dip. Temporary or not? I don't know but in any case, my hypothesis is that Google's AI tools may be replacing some search advertising opportunities faster than new revenue streams can compensate. Alphabet's latest earnings give that concern substance, but do not establish a net loss: Search revenue is still growing, and the company does not disclose enough Gemini economics to settle the question. Perhaps like you, I've been clicking fewer links in Google search results over the past year. That change in my own habits has made me wonder: if more of us get what we need from an AI answer, what happens to the business built around the searches and clicks that follow? The risk I see is that Google succeeds at changing how people find information, while weakening the economics that made its search business so valuable. The latest earnings give my hypothesis something concrete Alphabet's results for the quarter ended September 30, released October 28, showed Google Search & other revenue rising 12% to $63.35 billion. title: HYPE token skyrockets as NYSE owner moves to bring Hyperliquid perpetual futures to US traders
body: HYPE token is surging after Bloomberg reported that Intercontinental Exchange (ICE), the owner of the New York Stock Exchange, has joined forces with Trade.xyz to bring perpetual futures trading to US regulated markets using Hyperliquid's blockchain infrastructure. The proposed market would offer perpetual futures linked to equities, equity indexes, commodities and currencies. It would operate with its own clearing infrastructure, know-your-customer (KYC) procedures and anti-money-laundering (AML) controls, subject to regulatory approval. This represents a significant step toward bringing Hyperliquid's onchain derivatives model into traditional US financial markets. The partnership would significantly expand Hyperliquid's addressable market. The platform has established itself as a major venue for onchain perpetual futures, including contracts tied to traditional assets such as oil, gold and equity indexes. Bringing these products into a regulated US framework would attract more institutional participants and additional trading volume. Hyperliquid uses trading-fee revenue to fund purchases of its native token through its assistance fund. The proposed market should generate meaningful additional activity and contribute to the ecosystem's economics, strengthening the bullish case for the HYPE token. If you didn't know, you can get exposure to Hyperliquid through Hyperliquid Strategies, the Nasdaq-listed company associated with the HYPE treasury. The stock ticker is PURR.

title: ECB president Lagarde set to step down from her position next February
body: The statement notes that she has informed the ECB governing council of her decision to step down early and also conveyed that message to European Council president, Antonio Costa. On her successors, the ECB just noted that one "will be appointed by the European Council following the nomination process outlined in Article 283 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union". As a reminder, her tenure as ECB president is supposed to end in October 2027. So, leaving in February means she will be headed for an early departure by about six months. Now, speculation over Lagarde leaving the ECB early has been ongoing since the middle of 2025 already. At the time, Lagarde was heavily linked with taking over the WEF. Of course, she as well as the central bank were quick to try and play down such rumours back then. title: ECB preview: All Lagarde needs to do today is not rock the boat
body: The central bank bonanza this week continues as we move to Europe, with the ECB decision up next on the agenda today. After all the drama over the past day, we should likely get a much less exciting event later from the ECB later. The central bank is widely expected to leave key interest rates unchanged, with markets pricing in roughly 87% odds of a hold. That should keep the deposit rate at 2.50% following the 25 bps rate hike in September already. So barring any major surprises, the policy decision itself should be a relatively straightforward affair. The real question is whether ECB president Lagarde can get through her press conference without giving traders much of any reason to rethink December. Markets are currently pricing in around 64% odds of another rate hike by year-end. And I reckon policymakers will be quite comfortable in wanting to leave those expectations exactly where they are for now after today's decision. After all, inflation pressures are mounting in Europe during a time when fiscal risks are being thrust into the spotlight and growth momentum is beginning to slow down. Euro area headline annual inflation in September recorded a 3.8% while core annual inflation also remains stubborn at 2.5%, with services inflation keeping sticky at 3.2%. All of that just continues to make the case for further tightening even if energy prices continue to be the key driver in pushing up headline prices.

title: USDCHF tests key support as sellers challenge the 200-hour moving average
body: The USDCHF is trading near session lows after breaking below its 100-hour moving average at 0.82758. That break gave sellers the technical go-ahead to push lower, with the decline extending to 0.8257, right at the 200-hour moving average. The price has since edged back to around 0.8262, leaving traders with a clearly defined battle between buyers and sellers. The distinction between those two moving averages is important. The break below the 100-hour moving average shifted the near-term bias toward the sellers. However, reaching the 200-hour moving average introduces another decision point. Sellers have reached a downside target. To strengthen their control, they now need to break below that target and stay below it. For buyers, the same level offers an opportunity to define and limit risk. The buyer's perspective: Define risk before entry Why would a buyer step in when the price is falling? Because a technical trade does not require certainty that the market has bottomed. It requires a reason to enter, a clear point at which the trade idea is wrong, and enough potential reward to justify the risk. A buyer leaning against the 200-hour moving average near 0.8257 is looking for that level to attract support. If the price holds above it and begins to recover, the buyer benefits from entering close to support. If the price breaks below and selling gathers momentum, the reason for the trade weakens, giving the buyer a nearby reference point for exiting.

title: Gold slips below its 100-hour MA as interest-rate concerns weigh on the recovery
body: Fundamentally, and the recent him broader view, gold's retreat from its August high reflects a market more concerned about higher interest rates than attracted to its protection against inflation and geopolitical uncertainty. Higher Treasury yields, a firm dollar and expectations of further Federal Reserve tightening have made it difficult for buyers to sustain a recovery. That highlights an important distinction for gold traders. Although gold is often viewed as an inflation hedge, higher inflation does not automatically translate into higher gold prices. If inflation leads investors to expect tighter monetary policy and higher yields, the interest-rate response can outweigh demand for inflation protection. Gold pays no interest, so higher yields increase the opportunity cost of holding the metal. A stronger dollar can add another headwind by making dollar-denominated gold more expensive for buyers using other currencies. body: The ECB kept interest rates unchanged as expected, but President Christine Lagarde delivered a hawkish message despite the decision to hold. The decision to wait reflected unchanged underlying inflation and uncertainty surrounding the outlook, rather than a declaration that the tightening cycle was over. For EURUSD, the decision and press conference produced volatile trading. An initial decline took the price below the double bottom near 1.11135, established on October 14 and revisited yesterday. However, sellers could not sustain the break. After reaching 1.1106, the pair reversed higher and rebounded toward 1.1155. That recovery brought the price into a familiar swing area, with the falling 100-hour moving average just above. The failed break lower gives buyers an opportunity, but getting through resistance is the next requirement. A hawkish hold keeps the next meeting in focus Lagarde stressed that holding rates at this meeting does not rule out an increase at the next. Underlying inflation remains a key policy barometer, while elevated energy prices and geopolitical developments continue to complicate the outlook. The distinction matters. A central bank can leave rates unchanged while still delivering a hawkish message if its guidance keeps further tightening in play.
